is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles amharicus and Anopheles arabiensis (Anopheles gambiae s.l. complex) in Ethiopia.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for the Vgsc L995F (kdr-west) marker (page 6, 9).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper reports the number of mosquitoes genotyped for kdr-west (n=141) and provides the results (none were positive for the mutation) on page 9.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from the field in the Arjo-Didessa sugarcane irrigation area, Ethiopia (page 3, 4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original empirical research article.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies the Arjo-Didessa sugarcane irrigation area, Oromia Region, Ethiopia (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The collection period is explicitly stated as September to November 2019 (page 3, 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new collection of mosquitoes in 2019.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including sample sizes and results, are provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study investigated insecticide resistance in Anopheles amharicus and Anopheles arabiensis from the Arjo-Didessa sugarcane irrigation area in Ethiopia. The study performed WHO susceptibility tests and genotyped 141 mosquitoes for the kdr-west (L1014F) mutation. No kdr-west mutations were detected in the samples.
